It states he 'served 20 years in the USAF and worked as a Project Manager in the DOD until his 2001 retirement'.

claims.source: Reasoning over the two Andrew Johnson posts of 12 and 13 January 2015 compared against the decoration citations in the self-published collection; research/leads/verified-tr3b-2026-09-18.md section 5.3
claims.text: Stated inference. Taking Andrew Johnson's description of the FOIA return at face value, it corroborates the ordinary career and is silent on everything contested: no clearance record, no Groom Lake entry, nothing aerospace. A forgery allegation against the ordinary documents is therefore answered, and the aerospace claims are untouched, because the aerospace claims never rested on documents in the first place.
claims.unresolved: the board's own inference; it names no source that resolves

conflicts: Three different figures for the length of his career circulate and are not the same figure. His own 1998 presentation says 'My Career Background Spans 30 Years' and, separately, 'As a civilian, from 1987 to 1995, I performed as Engineering Program Manager, Site Manager, and Director of Engineering for several DoD Contractors'. The Find a Grave summary of the funeral home obituary says twenty years in the USAF plus DoD project management to a 2001 retirement. The three are reconcilable but none was reconciled from an opened record.

The temporary duty dates on the AF Form 77a, 1 June to 14 August 1979, extend past 16 July 1979, which is the date Andrew Johnson gives as the close of the Nellis assignment in the FOIA return. Temporary duty running concurrently with, and past the nominal end of, a permanent assignment is normal, but the overlap is recorded here rather than smoothed over, because the FOIA return itself was not opened and the two records were therefore never compared directly.

label: Edgar Fouche
narrative: Edgar Albert Fouche is the single named origin of the TR-3B account, and what makes him a node is that origin and not any documented authority. The ordinary facts of his life are settled at Tier 1: born 22 February 1948 in Americus, Georgia, died 11 May 2017 aged 69, buried at Coffey Cemetery in Mason County, Texas, and independently fixed at 1948 by the Library of Congress name authority attached to his own book. The career the opened records document is a twenty year enlisted avionics maintenance career: F-15 and F-16 manual test stations, the TEWS-TITE electronic warfare bay, a Strategic Air Command liaison post at Kelly AFB, a Community College of the Air Force associate degree in avionics systems technology, and three Meritorious Service Medals whose citations describe exactly that work. It is an honourable record and an entirely ordinary one, and nothing in it touches aerospace design, propulsion or physics. Everything extraordinary rests on his own word in documents he wrote and copyrighted himself: the Top Secret and 'Q' clearances, the descent from Napoleon's minister of police, the helicopter flights to Groom Lake, and the TR-3B. One document is a real counterweight and the node must carry it: an AF Form 77a of 24 August 1979 records him assigned temporary duty to AFFTC Detachment 3 on the Nellis range for ten weeks, and Peter Merlin, the historian whose analysis demolishes most of the rest of the account, is the source that identifies Detachment 3 AFFTC as the unit operating Groom Lake. That form also says its own limit out loud: his duties there 'have been verified via a separate report', and that separate report is not in the file. In July 1998 he published a novel with Brad Steiger; the Library of Congress catalogues it as science fiction. In August 1998 he gave the presentation that put the TR-3B into the world.

timeline.label: Edgar Albert Fouche dies, aged 69; buried Coffey Cemetery, Mason County, Texas
timeline.text: Find a Grave memorial 180498305, created 18 June 2017 and citing an obituary from Mason Funeral Home, gives the death date and age and the burial at Coffey Cemetery, Streeter, Mason County, Texas, with the inscription 'Saved by the blood of Jesus Christ'. A death date of 6 May 2018 at age 82 also circulates and is wrong on both counts; no opened record supports it.

unverified: That he ever stood at an International UFO Congress podium. The contemporaneous programme for the 7th Annual International UFO Congress Convention gives dates of 1 to 7 February 1998 at the Gold River Resort, Laughlin, Nevada, and its speaker list of 24 names does not include him. His own transcript is headed 'Copyright Aug. 1998' and his own text says he spoke at Laughlin 'in August'. The International UFO Congress ran summer sessions separately from its February convention, so August is consistent rather than contradictory, but no contemporaneous programme, report, ticket or press notice placing him on any podium in 1998 was opened. The venue attribution rests on his own document and on later repetition of it.

Any recorded admission by him that he lied. The arvp.co.uk TR-3B page asserts 'Jeremy Rys found him to have lied in his talk. He said he was pressured by people at iUFOC to mention S4'. No page or video authored by Jeremy Rys about Fouche was opened. The video said to record an admission is David Hilton's, and the only account of it that was opened says its screen could not be read: 'The video is about an alleged Skype conversation with Edgar Fouche, but I could not see the screen clearly enough in Hilton's video to verify the claims he was making'. The Paracast thread titled 'Ed Fouche comes clean - He is a liar and fraud!' contains no confession; its opening post is 'He is simply a faker.' No confession is in evidence anywhere in the opened record.

His screen credits. IMDb returned HTTP 403 to this environment on both the mobile and desktop hosts. The Union Pictures documentary he names in the presentation, and its broadcast date, were not opened, so his own claim that his documents were shown in it is uncorroborated.

A death date of 6 May 2018 at age 82 surfaced in a search result during this research and is wrong on both counts. No opened record supports it. It is recorded here so that a later session does not re-import it.
